statusDetail: Coverage complete across 58 atomic checks and five representative paths. Live comment submission was excluded as destructive; the associated validation-only check was explicitly not applicable.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with adaptive desktop/mobile templates
page.notes: Representative coverage: homepage/ranking, new listing, topic detail/comment surface, search results and 404 recovery. Account/checkout surfaces do not exist in the public journey. Not covered: destructive live comment/topic publishing, exhaustive historical topics, native apps.

checkOutcomes.method: Screenshot under dark emulation plus computed styles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark preference leaves light surfaces unchanged.
getAnimations() returned zero and no auto-advance or non-essential motion was visible.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and preference screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Several text styles fail WCAG contrast and there is no contrast-mode adaptation.
No view-transition declarations or transition animations were found for route/state changes.
No scroll-linked animation or custom animated scrollytelling exists, so no main-thread scroll animation anti-pattern was observed.
The site relies on native page scrolling and link activation; no custom pointer gesture that fights platform behaviour was observed.
The 139,047px topic page has static chrome and no progress/scroll-state response.
No tooltip, popover or anchored menu was present on the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchored overlay exists to position.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Pagination/list-to-topic changes have no directional transition or destination highlight, and overlapping mobile tabs weaken orientation.
No full-screen popup, consent wall or content-obscuring interstitial appeared on load.
No transient modal overlay was triggered in tested flows; disclosures and navigation remained ordinary document content.
The visual frame is simple and topic/list content occupies the main surface without ornamental application chrome.
Topic overflows by 88px and list navigation overlaps at narrow width.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed/CSS probe plus reused component screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: No container-responsive component was found and reused ranking/new tabs visibly collide at 360px.
Many links remove focus outlines; pagination targets measure 34x28px.
Ranking, new topics, search and comment actions are visible and Japanese labels make each template purpose clear.

checkOutcomes.method: Listing to topic and search results walkthrough
checkOutcomes.evidence: Users can open topics, paginate comments and complete a search without an account wall or dead end.
The 404 state explains the problem and provides a prominent return-to-top action.
Lighthouse LCP is 8.6s and TBT 10,680ms; performance score is 0.28.

checkOutcomes.method: Layout-shift observer on homepage and topic
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage CLS was 0 and topic CLS was 0.0011, both in the good range.
TBT is 10,680ms in Lighthouse; trace also observed a 199ms long task.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against live script attributes
checkOutcomes.evidence: A non-deferred classic script, render-blocking CSS, uncached font and uncompressed script are present.
Estimated savings are 189KiB JS and 15KiB CSS; two large Google tag bundles appear in the Lighthouse load.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits, image and form probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Missing alt, unnamed links/iframes and unlabeled inputs were directly enumerated.
Pink on white is measured at 2.2:1 and other grey labels at 3.94:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Landmark audit and keyboard focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No main landmark and multiple focused links have no visible outline.
Tabs overlap dates/labels and topic content exceeds the viewport, harming reading and scanability.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse viewport audit and target measurement
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile markup disables user scaling and pagination targets are only 34x28px.
errors-in-console passed with no captured console errors.
Doctype/charset exist, but image accessibility/responsiveness is poor and asset structure causes multiple audits to fail.
Synchronous XHR and deprecated Topics API use were captured, and Inspector Issues failed.
Homepage and topic have descriptive titles; homepage has a substantive meta description.
Links use href and robots allows crawling, but mobile zoom is disabled and narrow content overflows.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP/raw metadata, robots and sitemap inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTP is 200, canonical is present, robots allows public pages and advertises a current sitemap index.
Open Graph/Twitter tags exist, but no JSON-LD structured entity was found for content/discussion templates.
HTTPS is used, but CSP/HSTS/nosniff are absent and two cookies are not Secure.
14 of 19 requests and 258,759 bytes are third-party; known trackers and 400-day cookies are active.
No geolocation/notification request and no authentication flow was present in scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public anonymous content/search flow has no authentication or permission request to assess.

checkOutcomes.evidence: HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all absent.
Raw HTML returned 200 with 100% content coverage; title, H1 and description survive without JavaScript.
Core MPA navigation and search rendered without fragile shell, cut-off overlay or async blank state.
No manifest is exposed; this is a public discussion/content MPA rather than an installable application.
checkOutcomes.reason: Offline installability is not necessary for this public content/community MPA.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The invalid route has clear Japanese error copy and a working route back to the homepage.
Desktop/topic variants return an empty html lang for Japanese content.
The scoped flows show Japanese-relative timestamps and no user-entered currency/calendar data requiring multi-locale formatting.
checkOutcomes.reason: The service is deliberately Japanese-only in the inspected scope and exposes no locale-switching or locale-sensitive transaction data.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No scheduling, cross-zone event or editable time concept exists in the representative journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: No cross-time-zone scheduling or date-entry task is present.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No consent wall, confirmshaming, forced subscription or disguised primary control appeared in the tested journeys.
Search has no invalid state and posting was not submitted to avoid publishing content to a live community.
checkOutcomes.reason: No safe, non-destructive validation failure exists; live comment submission was intentionally not performed.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Search and comment inputs lack labels and useful autocomplete metadata.
No checkout, subscription, account or authentication flow exists in the public anonymous journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No commercial or account-management flow is present.

checkOutcomes.evidence: 97 below-fold images are not lazy, with oversized/legacy/non-responsive assets.
Heavy unused JavaScript and analytics work produces 10.68s TBT for a text-focused page.
Third parties are 78% of transfer bytes and duplicate analytics bundles dominate script cost.
Content is fully available in raw HTML, but no agent action surface or developer intent for agent tooling is evident.
checkOutcomes.reason: This public discussion reader exposes no safe transactional capability that requires WebMCP tooling.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or inference feature exists, and on-device AI is not necessary to complete the core reading/search journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-facing inference task is part of the current product.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline and post-10x long-page scroll heap summaries
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, heap self-size changed from 37,604,766 to 37,681,075 bytes (~0.2%) and node count fell from 562,666 to 562,204, showing no unbounded retained growth.
Topic heap is ~37.6MB despite a very long comment page; homepage uses ~3.9MB JS heap with 4,659 live DOM elements, proportionate to the rendered feed.
The valid repeated-scroll run did not increase node count and total heap remained effectively flat; no accumulating DOM population was observed.

principleOutcomes.reason: All checks were judged not applicable to this site and scope.

paths.description: Homepage/ranking template, primary discovery journey; inspected desktop, narrow mobile, dark preference, raw HTML, network, performance and accessibility.
New-topic listing archetype, representing alternate list state and navigation.
High-traffic topic detail and comment-reading/posting archetype, including pagination and long-session behaviour.
Search results journey for query AI, covering search completion and filter/results state.
Invalid route used to inspect HTTP/error recovery state.

findings.summary: The interface is hard-coded to a light palette.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot remains white/beige/pink, while the computed root color-scheme is normal and body background is rgb(250, 243, 234).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surface/text/accent tokens through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving contrast in both themes.

findings.summary: Low-contrast text and controls fail the accessibility floor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility is 0.48 and reports contrast ratios as low as 2.2:1 for pink text on white, below the required 4.5:1; the page also has no contrast preference adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken pink and grey text tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast handling.

findings.summary: Listing, topic and pagination navigation swaps abruptly without directional continuity.
findings.evidence: The CSS/animation probe found no View Transition usage and no active animations across the listing and topic templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions for list-to-topic and pagination changes, with reduced-motion respected.

findings.summary: Very long pages provide weak position and attention cues.
findings.evidence: The topic detail is 139,047px tall, yet screenshots and CSS probes show no reading progress, scroll-state-aware chrome, or transition/highlight cue; navigation is static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact sticky reading/progress control and preserve/highlight the destination after pagination or reply navigation.

findings.summary: Core listing and topic components do not reliably reflow on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: At 360px, topic layout reports 448px scroll width (88px overflow). Homepage/new tabs overlap dates and each other, and topic links measured around 552px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths, use intrinsic grid/flex sizing and overflow-wrap, then make reused list/header components respond to their container.

findings.summary: Essential controls, images and page regions are not exposed cleanly to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility is 0.48: image-alt, link-name, frame-title and main-landmark audits fail. The image primitive found 99/100 sampled images missing alt, and search/comment controls lack labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a main landmark, explicit form labels, accessible names for icon links/iframes, and meaningful alt or alt="" for decorative thumbnails.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inadequate, and zoom is disabled on mobile.
findings.evidence: Focused links repeatedly compute to outline-style none and no box shadow; pagination targets are 34x28px. Lighthouse reports user-scalable=no/maximum-scale restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible ring, increase targets to at least 44x44 CSS px where practical, and remove zoom restrictions.

findings.summary: Mobile loading and main-thread responsiveness are critically slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance is 0.28 with LCP 8.6s, TBT 10,680ms and interactive 17.1s. The first-party trace corroborates a 199ms long task and 149ms TBT in a lighter run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile and remove synchronous/third-party work from startup, prioritize the LCP resource, and defer/chunk non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Resource delivery includes blocking, uncached and largely unused work.
findings.evidence: HAR shows a parser stylesheet, a non-deferred classic script, an uncompressed script and a font without cache headers; Lighthouse estimates 189KiB unused JS and 15KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Split by template, defer non-critical classic scripts, compress/cache static assets, and remove duplicated/unused analytics and discovery code.

findings.summary: Long listings eagerly load poorly described, non-responsive image assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit sampled 100 images: 97 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded, five are oversized, five use legacy formats and nearly all lack srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold thumbnails, generate AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, and avoid empty image requests.

findings.summary: Third-party integrations use deprecated and main-thread-hostile browser behaviour.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices is 0.58 and records synchronous XHR from adg-script-loader plus deprecated Topics API use; inspector issues also fail.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or update vendors that use synchronous XHR/deprecated APIs and gate non-essential ad/analytics integrations.

findings.summary: Topic entities lack machine-readable structured data.
findings.evidence: The content is fully server rendered and has social tags, but the DOM probe finds no JSON-LD on the homepage and no structured entity evidence for the inspected topic.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org DiscussionForumPosting/BreadcrumbList JSON-LD aligned with visible topic metadata.

findings.summary: The HTTPS response omits all major defensive security headers and analytics cookies are insecurely scoped.
findings.evidence: Headers audit finds no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Both 400-day analytics cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer and minimal permissions policies; mark HTTPS cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party work dominate the small content-page transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR records 14/19 requests and 258,759/332,623 transferred bytes as third-party; tracker evidence finds Google Analytics/Tag Manager and Teads, with 400-day analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit necessity, load analytics only after the relevant consent basis, shorten retention, and remove redundant tags/vendors.

findings.summary: Some served templates omit the document language.
findings.evidence: Desktop homepage DOM and the topic probe return an empty html lang despite Japanese content; this impairs pronunciation and language detection.
findings.suggestedFix: Set <html lang="ja"> consistently on every desktop and mobile template, and retain language metadata through variants.

findings.summary: Search and comment inputs lack labels and useful autofill/input assistance.
findings.evidence: Search text input has no label, aria-label or autocomplete; topic textarea, file/name/url controls are also largely unlabeled and have empty autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels, search/name autocomplete tokens, input purpose attributes and contextual help without relying on placeholder text.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript is disproportionate to the core text-listing experience.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 78% of captured transferred bytes; Lighthouse loads two large Google tag bundles and estimates 189KiB unused JavaScript while TBT reaches 10.68s.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/CPU budget, consolidate analytics, and defer ads/discovery code until it approaches the viewport or user intent is clear.

taskList.title: Remove startup third-party/main-thread bottlenecks and prioritize LCP
Repair mobile reflow, component sizing, focus targets and zoom
Establish accessible names, labels, landmarks, alt text and contrast
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie/privacy defaults
Lazy-load and responsively encode listing images
Remove deprecated vendor APIs and synchronous XHR
Add long-page position cues and optional directional transitions
Set Japanese document language consistently and add topic JSON-LD
